template: On the open dashboard '{{v1}}' (URL /d/{{v3}}/...), do two things and save: (1) Add the tag 'bench' to the dashboard — open the dashboard settings (gear icon) > General, and add 'bench' as a tag, then save settings. (2) Set the dashboard's time range to the last 6 hours: open the time picker in the top bar and choose '{{v4}}'. Then SAVE the dashboard explicitly via the top-bar Save dashboard button, and in the save dialog TICK the checkbox 'Update default time range' so the 6-hour range is persisted into the saved dashboard, then confirm the save. Verify the save succeeded (a '{{03-open.save_confirmation_alert}}' confirmation appears) and report: the tag shown in dashboard settings, the time range shown in the top bar, and whether the 'Update default time range' checkbox was ticked.

reportTemplate.summary: Completed the instruction. The tag 'bench' was already added in Settings > General (verified live: a "Remove \"bench\" tag" control is present, screenshot /tmp/{{v2}}-settings-tag-bench.png). I then opened the top-bar time picker and selected '{{v4}}' (the previous attempt had left it on 'Last 12 hours'), clicked the top-bar 'Save dashboard' button, and in the save dialog I TICKED the 'Update default time range' checkbox — this was observed directly in the save dialog at save time (the action's state diff showed the checkbox as [checked] and the Save button changing from disabled to enabled); the dialog is now closed so it is not readable on the current page. Clicking Save produced a 'Dashboard saved' confirmation alert. Final verification on the dashboard page: the top bar shows 'Time range selected: {{v4}}', the URL carries from=now-6h&to=now, and both panels ('{{v2}} Notes' with content 'Notes for run {{v2}} — benchmark dashboard.' and '{{v2}} Availability') are intact (screenshot /tmp/{{v2}}-final-6h-saved.png).
